# GEO report: Millstone Bakery

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 100/100, Strong

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 23 ÷ 23 × 100 = 100. High = (23 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 100.

All 10 applicable rules are Clear, read from code. This is a small static HTML site with 4 pages, so the code answers almost everything. Only things outside the repository, such as a CDN or firewall, are unknown.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

No problems turned up, so these are the biggest unknowns.

### 1. Confirm real crawlers get through your hosting
- **Why it matters:** Code can't show whether a CDN or firewall blocks search and AI crawlers, even when robots.txt allows them.
- **Where:** hosting or CDN settings, which aren't in this repository
- **What the code says:** `robots.txt:2`: `Allow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 100–100 whether it comes back clear or not. Every rule is already scored from code, so this checks the live site, not the score.

### 2. Run a live scan once the site is deployed
- **Why it matters:** It checks real status codes, redirects and headers, which code can't prove.
- **Where:** the deployed site
- **What the code says:** `sitemap.xml:3`: `<loc>https://www.millstonebakery.example/</loc>`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** the code score stays at 100. The live score is reported separately.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and reachable | Clear | `robots.txt` has valid lines and is tiny |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers have the access your policy intends | Clear | `robots.txt:1-3` only blocks `/members/`. GPTBot (a training crawler) is blocked, matching `trainingCrawlers: block` |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Clear | 3 of 3 public routes indexable. `members/index.html:9` noindex is deliberate and not in the sitemap |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical on your own domain | Clear | all 4 pages have one on `www.millstonebakery.example` |
| GEO-003 | Main content is in server HTML | Clear | plain static HTML |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD (structured data) is valid | Not applicable | none found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Clear | `sitemap.xml`, `robots.txt:8` |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and html lang | Clear | 4 of 4 pages |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable through links | Clear | `<a href>` nav on every page |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | only `data-nosnippet` on one element (`breads.html:16`), which is a scoped choice |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | `index.html:16` image has alt. Pages sampled: all 4 |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | no app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt | Not scored | absent (information only) |
| GEO-102 | App structured data | Not scored | not an app |

## Other problems found

None found.

## Worth considering

Optional ideas. They aren't problems, and they don't change the score.

- **List the loaves on the breads page:** `breads.html:15`: `Over twenty loaves through the week, including our seeded rye and the country white.` Only two loaves are named. A list, or a page per loaf, would back up the claim and give readers and machines something to quote.
- **Add class details:** `classes.html:15`: `Book early, because places go quickly.` The page has no dates, price, group size or way to book. Add them as text.
- **Add address and opening hours:** `index.html:15`: `Pre-order for weekend collection.` No page gives the street address, hours or how to pre-order. Put them in text, and a `Bakery` or `LocalBusiness` JSON-LD block could label them.
- **Add Organization or WebSite structured data:** `index.html:10` has nothing after the canonical in `<head>`. A small block with the name, address and links would state the site's identity in machine-readable form.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `sitemap.xml:3-5`. None of the entries have dates.
- **Link between pages from the content:** `breads.html:15` and `classes.html:15` have no links onward. A link from breads to classes, or to a pre-order page, would help readers and crawlers.
- **Add social tags:** `index.html:7` sets a description but no `og:title`, `og:description` or `og:image`, so shared links will look plain.
- **Check the image file exists:** `index.html:16`: `src="/img/loaves.jpg"`. No `img/` folder is in the repository. If it isn't added at deploy, the image is broken.
- **Describe the opening headline:** `index.html:14`: `Sourdough baked in York every morning`. It's good, and the "wide range of loaves from heritage grains" line (`index.html:15`) could name which grains.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Server answers:** real status codes, redirects and headers for `/robots.txt`, `/sitemap.xml` and each page. A live scan settles these. They don't change any code result.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. `geo.config.json` says `aiSearchCrawlers: allow`.
- I read all 6 tracked files: 4 pages, `robots.txt`, `sitemap.xml` and `geo.config.json`. There is no `package.json`, no JSON-LD (searched all files), no build step and no other router.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command if you'd like help with any of the ideas above. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
